Short answer
Urge is Savant’s non-authoritative iteration and convergence engine. It applies revision pressure to candidate solutions, evaluates them against explicit criteria, drives bounded improvement cycles, and projects consensus/stability across competing candidates. It never mutates canon or creates authority; it produces deterministic, replayable projections with full lineage.

What that means in practice
- Role and authority
  - Entity: exile:urge (accepted; parent edifice:identity:4)
    - Evidence: canon-system/authority/exiles/urge.yaml
  - Purpose: iteration, improvement cycles, revision pressure
    - Evidence: canon-system/authority/exiles/urge.yaml
  - Boundaries: projection-only; no canon/source mutation; no truth claims
    - Evidence: capabilities and all runtime projections set authority_effect=none and projection_only=true
      - ontology/.../exiles/urge/interface/capabilities/capabilities.json
      - runtime projections below

- Public interface (declared contracts)
  - urge.iteration.job: input id/objective/payload/criteria → output best/alternates/lineage/failures/metrics/stop_reason/digest
  - urge.iteration.evaluator: input payload/context → output scores
  - urge.iteration.reviser: input payload/pressure → output sequence of revised payloads
  - urge.iteration.composition: ties job+evaluator+reviser with policy and convergence interpretation
    - Evidence: ontology/.../exiles/urge/interface/contracts/contracts.json

- Core runtimes (what it actually does)
  1) Iterative improvement engine
     - File: ontology/.../exiles/urge/runtime/iteration.py
     - You define:
       - job: id, objective, payload, criteria (weighted targets; required flags)
       - evaluator(payload, context) → scores per criterion
       - reviser(payload, pressure) → revised candidate payloads
     - Engine.run():
       - Evaluates initial payload, then cycles: revision → evaluation → selection
       - Deterministic ranking by required_met, weighted score, tie-breakers
       - Policies: max_cycles, branch_factor, min_improvement, target_score, patience, max_candidates, etc.
       - Produces: best, alternates (top-k), lineage (all candidates with parent links and assessment digests), failures, metrics, stop_reason, digest
       - Strict canonical-JSON digestion to ensure replayability

  2) Job adapter boundary (decouples execution from engine)
     - File: ontology/.../exiles/urge/runtime/job_adapter.py
     - execution_boundary(evaluate, revise, identity): sync callouts that execute your actual scoring and revision logic
     - adapter wraps that boundary into evaluator/reviser objects the engine accepts
     - Adds request/response digests; enforces shapes; disallows async inside urge

  3) Convergence and stability projection (textual candidate consensus)
     - Convergence (token Jaccard, anchor selection, consensus tokens, pairwise similarities, ranked list)
       - File: runtime/convergence.py
     - Stability (signals derived from convergence: stability, ambiguity, separation, dispersion, pairwise mean)
       - File: runtime/stability.py
     - Policy normalization and interpretation (thresholds for “stable/ambiguous/strongly_separated”)
       - File: runtime/convergence_policy.py (normalize, interpret)
     - Composition wrapper projects both and links lineage
       - File: runtime/composition.py

  4) Creative orchestration (diverge → discriminate → synthesize → discriminate)
     - File: runtime/creative_orchestration.py
     - External integrations:
       - Provider orchestration via Opus execute_text_request_resilient
         - Import: .../opus/runtime/resilient_text
       - Structural discrimination via Underscore Vessel (novelty/divergence, anti-cliché, MMR frontier)
         - Import: .../underscore/runtime/vessel/vessel
     - Process:
       - Divergence: multiple “lenses” prompt passes with provider; normalize, dedup, id candidates
       - Discrimination: Vessel ranks, rejects cliché/false-diversity, selects a frontier
       - Synthesis: adversarial synthesis prompts over frontier to create structurally novel candidates
       - Final discrimination: recompute frontier; output candidates, frontiers, lineage and ownership map
     - Boundaries: projection-only; preserves provider and selection lineage; deterministic IDs
